pull_requests.title: Alternating own-curvature bounds clear cold trajectory without LR decay; cold ring still fails
pull_requests.body: Follow-up to #60 continuous-learning research. **Cold trajectory is cleared without LR decay. Warm and cold ring each pass separately, but no candidate passes both.** Nothing is eligible for production and there is no 22/22 claim. Production defaults are untouched. ## Key finding: simultaneous-update confound Every earlier recorder-based game update evaluated D and G at one joint point, i.e. a simultaneous game. The real host alternates. With all bounds off: - the simultaneous scaffold fails cold trajectory (MSE .228); - plain alternating constant Adam passes it (.00295). The new alternating adapter reproduces plain alternating Adam bit-for-bit on both hosts. ## Mechanism Same-sample own-curvature ratio per player: rho = ||sqrt(P) ΔF_own|| / ||Δ/sqrt(P)||. Each player's step is scaled by min(1, c/rho). The update is fully alternating, advances moments once per player, verifies RNG replay, and never reads the target. ## Stencil-critic line (#84 recipe frozen as the base) | Run | Warm | Cold trajectory | Cold ring | |---|---|---|---| | v16 = #84 recipe | 196/200 | PASS .00094 | **PASS**, 8 modes | | v17: G curvature on the plain critic | **200/200** | PASS | FAIL, 7 modes | | v18: pre-bound per-sample slope weights | 192/200 | — | — | | v19: post-bound step × min(1, particle slope) | **200/200** | PASS | FAIL, max 7 modes | | v20: post-bound step × slope only while slope < .2 | 199/200 (1175) | — | — | **v20:** at rest the particle slope wanders .14–.24. When it crossed .2 at updates 1171–1173, the gate opened, full #84 steps followed, and a mode was lost at 1175. The threshold is fragile at rest. **The rest-damping family is closed.** Continuous damping trades warm against ring, pre-bound weighting is cancelled by the curvature bound, and a hard gate leaks at threshold crossings. ## Earlier rows (warm 200/200 unless stated) | Variant | Cold trajectory | Cold ring | |---|---|---| | v10: G .25, D 3 | PASS .00094 | 3/5 terminal checks | | v11 / v14 | FAIL ~.25 | — | | v12 / v13 / v15 | PASS | FAIL | Hold ≥2400 was not run. ## Visuals Gray = the 8 mode centers with the .21 HQ radius; color = the 12 generator particles. ![v10 cold ring (D bound 3)](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-1456070c-7f64-4c2c-904f-12c803286df9) ![v8 cold ring](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-2adb586b-19ea-41e7-a464-be2086acff58) ![v6 cold ring (collapses)](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-8ba12286-5bff-469e-b096-221ec074e5f6) Reports: `reports/toy100/alternating-curvature-report.md` and `reports/toy100/cross-curvature-report.md`. Evidence is under `reports/toy100/continuous-evidence/alternating-curvature/`. Tests: 179 passed locally.

Slope max .25, so acquisition was damped too | | Hard gate: drop the G step only if slope < 0.2 | PASS 200/200, min HQ .999 | PASS .000943, suffix 18 | FAIL. 8 modes and HQ ≥ .96 at 1000–1150, then 5 modes / .443 at 1200. pull_requests.title: Capped Monge prior step on the PR84 continuous-learning candidate
pull_requests.body: ## Hypothesis The cold ring stalls at 7 modes because the missing mode sits behind a critic-score valley. Voronoi centroids (coverage, Chamfer) and Sinkhorn barycentric drift average a surplus particle into that valley. A minimum-cost bijection to 12 farthest-point real representatives was meant to assign one particle onto uncovered mass and leave its partner on the occupied mode. Each prior step is capped at 0.2 in output space and accepted only if that frozen assignment cost falls. Trajectory would keep the original PR84 path. Literature: Monge map versus Kantorovich barycentric projection (Peyré & Cuturi). He et al. 2026 Sinkhorn drifting (arXiv:2603.12366) is barycentric and already failed the fixed-cloud proxy in `nonlocal-signal-filter.md`. ## Result — stopped at warm PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu, one thread (not the cu126 archive). Same-process controls: identity 200/200, constant Adam 4/200, correction-disabled PR84 **196/200** (min HQ .866, final 8/.999). That PR84 score matches the published warm miss, not the cu126 200/200 replay. The Monge arm is **0/200**, final 8 modes / HQ .652. Every proposal accepted at α=1. On the first update, 7 of 12 particles were matched 2.15–2.33 away and walked 0.20. Latent norm was 0.37 with rank-2 Jacobians, so this is not the Chamfer latent explosion. Twelve farthest-point targets have a different occupancy than twelve particles that already cover eight modes, so the bijection orders covered particles onto other modes. Cold trajectory, ring, and hold were not run. | Method | Warm | Cold trajectory | Cold ring | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Capped Monge bijection, output cap 0.2, on PR84 | **FAIL 0/200** | not run | not run | ## Handoff A balanced bijection cannot rest on a matched 12-to-8 cloud and also walk one particle into an empty mode: any target occupancy that differs from the particles forces a mode-scale move. Unbalanced nearest-neighbor targets were already tested. No cap sweep. The selected partial candidate remains the original PR84 stencil. Write-up: `reports/toy100/monge-assignment-report.md`.

pull_requests.title: Reject reverse-KL + chi-squared KDE drift as an LR-decay replacement
pull_requests.body: ## Result **Does not qualify.** One reverse-KL + chi-squared KDE drift (Cao & Wei, arXiv:2603.10592), pulled back onto the PR84 prior, fails the dense warm fork. Cold trajectory, ring, and the 2400 hold were not run. ## Why this lever The missing ring mode is a local critic barrier, and forward-KL drifting was already the suggested next kernel test. This arm uses the paper's other mixture: velocity `(p/q + q/p)(m_p - m_q)`, which upweights uncovered data (reverse KL) and surplus generated mass (chi-squared). Bandwidth is the max real-to-nearest-particle gap. Output steps are capped at 0.1 and latent steps at 1. No mode centers, clock, or rest gate. ## Evidence | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | Identical clouds | Drift 0 | | Clean covered 12-on-8 cloud, 200 steps | 8 modes / HQ 1 the whole way | | Clean missing mode | Recovers 8 / HQ 1 by step 22–24, but HQ hits 0 mid-way | | Warm identity | 200/200, final 8 / .999 | | Warm PR84, correction off (this torch 2.14 CPU) | 196/200, misses 1129–1132, final 8 / .999 | | Warm mixture | 173/200, steps 1174–1200 fail, final **2 / .201** | All 200 mixture proposals were accepted. Bandwidth median .26, max 2.47. A far real widens the global kernel, the mixture energy falls, and covered modes are abandoned. That is the same transient the clean missing-mode cloud already showed, and the every-step warm gate rejects it. The correction-off arm is not bit-identical to the archived torch 2.13 warm pass (200/200). The mixture is still worse than that arm in the same process. ## Tests `tests/test_chi_mixture_pullback.py`: 3 passed (exact rest, capped energy decrease, rejected-step restoration). Details: `reports/toy100/chi-mixture-drift-report.md`. ## Recommendation Do not grid bandwidths or caps on this global kernel. The width that sees a missing mode (~2.3) is the width that leaves covered modes. A force that is zero on reals already inside a within-mode radius was not tested here.

pull_requests.title: Refreshed Chamfer targets fail the 2400 continuation
pull_requests.body: ## Summary Acquisition-target quality, not another generator rest damper. Four nearest-neighbor refreshes of the current real minibatch, then a prior-only Gauss-Newton landing onto that frozen target. Actual unit-mean Chamfer must decrease or the prior is restored. No target centers and no coefficient sweep. The same-target continuation is the failing gate. Warm 200/200 is not enough: updates 2240 and 2250 drop to 6 modes while the final checkpoint is still 8 modes / HQ .99976. ## Gates | Gate | Result | | --- | --- | | Identity, scheduled, through 2400 | 200/200 then 120/120, exact cold-host parity | | Refreshed candidate, 1001–1200 | **200/200**, min HQ .94360 | | Same branch, every 10 steps through 2400 | **118/120 FAIL** at 2240 (6 / .91675) and 2250 (6 / .91162) | | Cold trajectory and ring | Run before the new order. Trajectory MSE .00094267 PASS. Ring terminals 1000–1200 all 8 modes, HQ .975–1. **Not a promotion.** | Stopped after the continuation failure. No acquired-state hold. Details: `reports/toy100/refreshed-chamfer-continuation.md`. ## Why this rule On captured states, landing exactly on the one-step Chamfer target still missed modes. Four assignment refreshes covered 8 modes. The existing linear pullback did not reach that cloud. Gauss-Newton did. That isolated filter is why the live rule refreshes assignments before the nonlinear step. PR84's original stencil remains the reference partial result. It already failed this continuation (first observed fail at 1390). This candidate only moves the loss later.

pull_requests.title: Critic-value spare step fails the 2400 hold
pull_requests.body: ## Summary A critic-value spare-particle pull, aimed at the ring's local gradient barrier, does not fix delayed same-dataset instability. On PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu it passes the dense warm window, then misses 8 of 120 continuation checks through update 2400. The final checkpoint is 8 modes / HQ .999 and hides those misses. Not a production replacement. ## What was searched - Closed and left alone: rest-damping, Monge/Sinkhorn, path-crossing, χ²-KDE, Chamfer and one-sided coverage pullbacks, target-center oracles, critic EMA, time-boxed loosening, HQ latches. - Read [Gradient Flow Drifting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.10592) and [drifting as score matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.09936). The chosen lever uses the critic **value** gap (the missing mode is the highest score while the local gradient points away) with a 0.1 output trust region, instead of a latent Chamfer pseudoinverse or a slope rest-gate. ## Numbers (this CPU, seed 0) Warm-state hash `57c10b57…`, not the archived cu126 hash `6cc79b6e…`. Local PR84 is therefore not the archived 1390 episode. | Run | Warm 1001–1200 | Checks 1210–2400 | Worst later | Final | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | | Scheduled identity | 200/200 | 120/120 | 8 / .998 | 8 / .998 | | Constant Adam | 4/200 | 10/120 | 3 / .028 | 8 / .828 | | PR84, correction off | 196/200 | 114/120 | 7 / .829 | 8 / 1 | | Value spare step | 200/200 | **112/120** | 7 / .830 | 8 / .999 | Value failures: 1270, 1280, 1520, 1820, 2090, 2100, 2180, 2390. The pull fired twice and was accepted both times; it was off during the dips. A separate cold run (done before the hold-first priority) passed trajectory MSE .000943 and ring 8 / HQ .970 at update 1200. That does not meet the continuation gate. ## Why The dips happen while `max D(real) - mean D(fake)` stays inside two real-score standard deviations. A value-gap gate rests through the drift. Do not tune that threshold. Next: attribute the proposal at the first failing check (1270 here, 1390 on the archived continuation). Details: `reports/toy100/value-transport-hold-report.md`.

pull_requests.title: Tighten open-cap PR84 steps using the PR #92 rho split
pull_requests.body: Frozen PR84 stencil, bounds .25/3, alternating host. No rest-slope damp, no mode center, no gate change. Cold was not run. ## Why this rule PR #92 verdict B on this build: 674 useful acquisition steps, all with the cap closed, minimum rho .538, median 1.83. Clean HQ exits have median rho .217. Every open-cap exit has rho ≤ .25. A cut at rho < .538 catches 33/34 exits and 0/674 acquisition steps. Warm is 196/200 at 1129–1132. The .080 step at 1129 is not the boundary particle. Update 1130 leaves with the cap already closed. The same-machine hold is 114/120. PR84's factor is `min(1, 0.25 / rho)`, which is 1 for every rho ≤ .25. The extra scale is `rho / 0.25` only in that open band. The applied factor is `min(rho / 0.25, 0.25 / rho)`. It equals 1 at the existing bound and does not change steps with rho ≥ .538. ## Same-machine results | Rule | Warm | Min HQ | Hold to 2400 | Worst hold | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Scheduled identity | 200/200 | .990 | 120/120 | 8 / .998 | | PR84 | 196/200 | .866 | 114/120 | 7 / .829 | | Nearest-real exit clip | 200/200 | .939 | 117/120 | 8 / .808 | | Open-cap rho tighten | 200/200 | .959 | 115/120 | 8 / .784 | Rho failures: 1630, 1960, 2160, 2200, 2280, all 8 modes, minimum HQ .784. The margin clip's failures were 1490, 1590, 2280, minimum HQ .808. It cleared warm 200 and beat 114/120, so it stays on the record. It is not 120/120. ## Kill Both rules beat 114/120 and neither holds 120/120. The rho band is the split #92 measured, and HQ still drops after the warm window. Stop. No threshold sweep and no cold gate. Detail: `reports/toy100/exit-aware-rho-report.md`.

Every useful cold-ring step has rho ≥ 0.538. Twenty-three clean HQ exits have the cap open (rho ≤ 0.25), and zero useful acquisition steps do. A cut at rho < 0.538 keeps 33 of 34 exits and none of the 674 acquisition steps. The exception is one closed-cap exit at rho 0.554 (update 2361). Receipts: `reports/toy100/continuous-evidence/pr84-open-cap-diagnosis/report.md`. ## Reproduction torch 2.14.0+cpu, Python 3.12.3, AVX2. Adapter sha256 `9c17b1b0…f0111f` (the selected candidate). Warm-state sha256 `57c10b57…c48861`. | Gate | Result | | --- | --- | | Warm 1001–1200 | 196/200. First fail 1129–1132. Minimum HQ .8662, 8 modes | | Hold every 10 through 2400 | 114/120. Fails 1720, 1840, 1900, 2110, 2290, 2370. Worst 7 modes / HQ .829 | | Cold ring, this build | Terminal 8 modes / HQ .9988. This does not replace the archived 7-mode ring | This is the PR #90 1129 event, not the archived 1390 event. Update 1390 is not a graded failure here. ## First failure, proposal vs applied Update 1129 grades eval HQ .899 with 8 modes. The cap is open (rho .171, factor 1), so proposal and applied output motion match. Clean HQ stays 1. No clean particle leaves. Particle 1 is the closest: margin .010 → .000, step .011. pull_requests.title: Restore spent nearest-real margin on the PR84 exit clip
pull_requests.body: Frozen PR84 stencil, bounds .25/3, alternating host. Starts from the nearest-real exit clip in PR #91, not the open-cap rho tighten. No rest-slope damp, no mode center, no gate change. Cold was not run. ## Why this rule PR #91 nearest-real clip: warm 200/200, hold 117/120, failures 1490, 1590, 2280, worst 8 / HQ .808. The clip fired at update 2280 (`clipped=1`, `min_scale=0.0007`) and still graded HQ .866. Freezing an outward step leaves a particle that is already past the fence outside the HQ ball (radius 3×0.07 ≈ .21; fence ≈ .08). Rho-only cannot cover that class: PR #92 shows update-1130 exits with the cap already closed and margin about 0, and the open-cap tighten held 115/120. The extension does not read rho. After the unchanged .25 cap: - A particle still inside whose step would cross the fence is shortened to the fence. - A particle already past the fence whose step would increase nearest-real distance is placed on the fence along the ray to its nearest real. Inward steps and interior steps stay on PR84. ## Same-machine results torch 2.14.0+cpu, one prefix, constant rates .00425 / .00425 / .0085 after update 1000. | Rule | Warm | Min HQ | Hold to 2400 | Worst hold | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | Scheduled identity | 200/200 | .990 | 120/120 | 8 / .998 | | PR84 | 196/200 | .866 | 114/120 | 7 / .829 | | Nearest-real exit clip (#91) | 200/200 | .939 | 117/120 | 8 / .808 | | Open-cap rho tighten (#91) | 200/200 | .959 | 115/120 | 8 / .784 | | Fence restore | 200/200 | .965 | **119/120** | 8 / .891 | The single miss is update 2160 (8 modes, HQ .891). That update has no exit-clip event; 2159 and 2161 do. It is not an outward crossing of the minibatch fence. 1490, 1590, and 2280 are gone.
